problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-{3}^{x}+1?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-3({5}^{x})+2?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y=3({5}^{x}).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/9fb37b22dd1fdc3be207402b95d84e1bfae560eae2381978f76e3e4068e8811c.png)

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-3({5}^{x}).$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,3)$ to $(0,-3)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/be55692e10a722797da99b435c76f486cbcd211ed0d30b8c8785e8d96c88ef7b.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $2$ units up to give $y=-3({5}^{x})+2.$ The point $(0,-3)$ moves to $(0,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/c1a083f8412bc88725735d2ceca5b2e8eb08ef55584181419a76bec6c978d2e5.png)
